front.title: Stateless Server-Assisted Hole Punching for QUIC

abstract.t: This document specifies a QUIC extension that lets two endpoints connected through a relay establish a direct path between them when one or both are behind Network Address Translators (NATs). The client asks the server, over the existing connection, to send a single small "punch" packet toward one of the client's address candidates. The server keeps no per-attempt state and does not initiate validation of candidate paths. After a short delay, the client validates the direct path using ordinary client-initiated path validation as defined in RFC 9000, or ordinary path creation as defined in RFC 10069 when QUIC multipath is in use, and can then migrate the connection to it.
